title: Transport of the actual pro-etale supported product through isomorphisms
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring and f:X→S,g:Y→S scheme morphisms with X,Y and X×_S Y locally Noetherian. Let i:Z→X,j:W→Y be closed immersions. For arbitrary unbounded pro-etale A-module complexes and specified isomorphisms K≅K′, L≅L′, invertibility of the actual pairing [def-pur-proetale-supported-exterior-product] for K,L implies invertibility for K′,L′. The maps are defined using the same normalized adjunctions and coefficient tensor comparisons.

source.place: Paragraph 4, naturality under the specified etale-origin witness isomorphisms

proof.text: The coefficient comparison is natural in its two derived module inputs by the first clause of its ComparisonFamilyCondition [lem-pur-derived-tensor-comparison]. The derived tensor presentation is identified with the curried monoidal tensor; transport this equality of Hom families before applying the naturality clause.

Each pulled-back evaluation is a composite of the exact-derived composition comparison, the coefficient adjunction counit and the derived-upper-star comparison. Naturality of these three natural transformations gives the evaluation squares for K→K′ and L→L′. Bifunctoriality of tensor then gives the square for the composite coefficient-comparison/evaluation map.

Apply naturality of the adjunction Hom equivalence to this square. Its left vertical map is the tensor of the supported-section images of the two given isomorphisms, and its right vertical map is the supported-section image of their external tensor. Functors preserve isomorphisms, so cancellation transfers invertibility of the adjunct. The final equality transport into the external-product presentation is itself invertible. This proof is entirely categorical and applies also to zero objects and empty supports.
